title: WearOS 'Apps on Your Phone' support being depricated by Google - XDrip WearOS functionality becoming un-usable
body:
Google is terminating support for Android-app-bundled WearOS watch-apps in-favor of requiring all watch-apps to be hosted on the Play Store.

XDrip uses the 'old method' (watch app bundled inside phone version), which means that XDrip WearOS support will break for new installs (and re-installs), as it will not be possible to install the WearOS xdrip app anymore.

Fix involves either:
A) breaking-out the WearOS app into it's own separately downloadable APK and posting it along with instructions on how to adb-sideload it *to the watch*
-or-
B) Getting it listed on the play-store.

I would tag it as bug if wearOS no longer works!

While a release to play would have the highest convenience factor, it's unrealistic.

If the build system would add the wear.apk signed with the same key, it would be possible to side load it. It needs to be signed with the same key in order to communicate with the phone.

Since this is my post originally, a thought:

What if the XDrip+ phone app was packaged with the required scripts/executables/etc to have a 'sideload app to watch' button in the app, which would then perform similar functionality to (http://feedproxy.google.com/~r/xda-developers/ShsH/~3/lLbxmCuZfV8/) but only for the xDrip+ watch-app rather than as a general purpose solution? 

Make it so that all a user has to do, is enable sideloading on the watch, then go into the XDrip phone-app's settings -> watch-settings -> 'Android Wear' menu, and click 'sideload app to watch'...

A FAQ entry on allowing ADB/side-loading permissions would be needed, of course.
